description: Camera-agent browser runtime — getUserMedia video preview, canvas frame capture, multimodal LLM POST, overlay rendering of text + optional bounding boxes.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any product where the primary input is the device camera: visual QA, barcode/QR readers, OCR tools, 'describe what you see' agents, webcam-based search, live inspection apps.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on the configured port; the browser will prompt for camera permission on first visit.
Point the camera, type a question, and press 'Capture + ask' — the frame is JPEG-compressed and POSTed to `/api/vision`.
Implement the backend described in `api/README.md` — any multimodal LLM endpoint accepting `{ image, prompt }` and returning `{ answer }` works.
Run `pnpm validate` to verify scaffold wiring without opening a browser.
Run `pnpm build` to emit a static bundle to `dist/` — deploy to any static host; HTTPS is required for `getUserMedia` outside localhost.
gotchas: `getUserMedia` requires HTTPS outside localhost — plain HTTP on any real hostname fails with `NotAllowedError` before the permission prompt appears.

iOS Safari auto-rotates camera frames based on device orientation but `canvas.drawImage` does not — on mobile portrait the JPEG is sideways. Always read `videoWidth/videoHeight` after `loadedmetadata` fires.
`canvas.toDataURL()` is synchronous and blocks the main thread on large frames. For >1080p, switch to `canvas.toBlob()` which runs off-thread and is ~3× faster.
Base64 JPEGs are ~1.33× their binary size. For high-res frames (>500 KB), send as `multipart/form-data` or use `toBlob()` + binary `fetch` to cut payload size.
The `MediaStream` keeps the camera LED on until every `track.stop()` is called — don't just pause `<video>`, call `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` on teardown.
architectureNotes: All browser logic lives in `src/main.ts` — camera lifecycle, frame capture, API call, and overlay rendering. Fork cleanly from there.
The hidden `#work` canvas captures frames; `#overlay` is the visible canvas that draws bounding boxes on top of the `#cam` video element.
Bounding box coordinates from the API are normalized 0..1 so they survive display-size rescaling — multiply by `overlay.width`/`overlay.height` to get pixel coordinates.

placeholders.description: Bootstrap camera agent. Implement the `/api/vision` backend described in `api/README.md`. Optionally replace the bounding-box overlay with custom rendering (heat maps, segmentation masks, etc.).
